adjudication_records.issue_text: public/app/plugins/datasource/loki/querySplitting.ts:299 — [P1, confidence 75] `.map((query) => datasource.applyTemplateVariables(query, request.scopedVars, request.filters))` applies templating a second time after `runShardSplitQuery` has already applied the same transform at `shardQuerySplitting.ts:52`, so a shard-split query whose first expansion contains another template token is expanded again and executes a different query than the one used to discover shards.

adjudication.rationale: The finding claims that runSplitQuery calls applyTemplateVariables after runShardSplitQuery has already applied it, causing double templating. However, looking at the diff, runSplitQuery (querySplitting.ts) and runShardSplitQuery (shardQuerySplitting.ts) are separate entry points - they don't call each other. runSplitQuery handles regular query splitting while runShardSplitQuery handles shard-based splitting. Each applies template variables once at their respective entry points. There's no evidence in the diff that one calls the other, so there's no double application of templating.

adjudication.rationale: The finding claims the code cannot type-check because there's no './datasource' module defining LokiDatasource. However, this is a test file and implementation file that receives 'datasource' as a parameter - it's passed in at runtime. The diff shows the code correctly calls datasource.applyTemplateVariables() which is a standard Grafana datasource method. The finding misunderstands how the code works - LokiDatasource is defined elsewhere in the codebase (not shown in this diff) and is passed as a parameter. The tests in the diff actually mock this method successfully, proving it exists and works.
